item: The swap window's cleanup passes one section of the state lock, so a failed exit of it no longer blocks the cleanup with the window held
refs: coordinator 17 Oct (option 2 on the _revive/_close_window plan); finding F3 of the independent read of PR #1435; PR #1440
summary: swap_window's cleanup passed three with-_STATE sections (the _DISK_CHANGED read, _revive, _close_window), so a failed exit of the first or the second (a plain lock left held; measured with the allocator on cold free lists, 3.13) blocked the next section of the SAME cleanup with the exclusive library window held and every new pooled connection waiting. They are now one section in _close_window(swapped, earlier=None); _revive is gone. A failed exit of that one still raises the error and the finally still gives the window back, but _STATE stays held and the NEXT swap blocks at its first section. The three opening sections (reset, bump, open) are the same exits and still block this swap's close (3 of 4 sections, from 5 of 6); merging them would only move the block. Said in swap_window's docstring and pinned by three tests. Red-without: an AST count of the sections in the cleanup (1; 3 on the module rewritten back) and a stand-in _STATE whose exit fails and stays held (old shape: blocked, window held; new: MemoryError, window given back, a connecting() gets through). Not here: dropping _STATE (a separate proof).
